what: Sabesp supplies water and sewerage to São Paulo state in Brazil, serving tens of millions of people. It was privatised in 2024, with the state government retaining a minority stake.
customers: Households, businesses and municipalities across São Paulo state.
moat: A monopoly over water and sewerage in Brazil's richest and most populous state, with tariffs set by a regulator under a long concession.
risks: Brazilian regulatory and political intervention in tariffs is a persistent risk
Drought reduces water availability and has forced rationing before
Large investment obligations to extend sewerage coverage
opportunities: Revenue grew about 19% a year over three years
Privatisation has allowed cost reductions that were impossible under state control
Analysts see about 37% upside, with a dividend yield near 6%
watch: Tariff reviews, operating cost reduction, and sewerage coverage targets.
